transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-04
Start time: 15:30 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE); Noah Kim (Redwood SE); Daniel Reed (Aurum CTO); Priya Shah (Head of ML); Owen Li (Infra)

Summary: quick discovery focused on unit economics for hosted vs dedicated vs private. Customer wants unit cost targets and levers (batching, prefix/KV caching, quantization) to hit budget. Discussed benchmarking, security, and next steps to run POC.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE at Redwood. With me is Noah, our solutions engineer. How are you all?
[00:12] Daniel (Aurum): Good, thanks. Yup, thanks for setting this up. We want to focus on cost — cost per inference token and what levers we have.
[00:22] Priya (Aurum): Yeah, primarily batching and caching. Also curious when Dedicated makes sense vs Hosted.
[00:28] Noah (Redwood): Great, that's exactly what we wanted to cover. Quick call outline: we'll ask about traffic patterns, targets, and constraints, then go through rough unit economics and levers (batching, KV cache, quantize), and then recommend next steps.
[00:45] Owen (Aurum): Sounds good. We're on a constrained budget — roughly $120k/month for LLM infra across teams, but that has to cover embeddings and generations.
[00:55] Maya (Redwood): Helpful. A couple quick qual questions — are you currently using any hosted LLM provider? Which models and what's avg sequence length?
[01:05] Priya (Aurum): We're prototyping on Anthropic and some open LLMs via Replicate, mixed. Avg generation 300 tokens, but embeddings workload is separate and heavier. Peak QPS is about 30 r/s, typical concurrency ~50 requests during bursts.
[01:20] Noah (Redwood): Ok that's useful. So ballpark: with hosted per-token pricing, the biggest levers for lowering unit cost are batching (higher throughput per GPU), KV/prefix caching for repeated contexts, and quantization/model selection.
[01:35] Daniel (Aurum): Curious about numbers — like if we do 300-token responses at 30 r/s, what's the per-token cost hosted vs dedicated?
[01:44] Maya (Redwood): We gave examples in our spreadsheet — I'll send it — but rough numbers: hosted (pay-as-you-go) for a 7B-ish open model might be $X per 1k tokens on our platform; Dedicated reserved instances with optimized batching and int8 quantization can reduce effective unit cost by 2-4x depending on hit rate for caching and batching profile. (transcription: "int-ate" -> int8 sometimes transcribed wrong)
[02:10] Priya (Aurum): Can you unpack the 2-4x? Where does that come from?
[02:15] Noah (Redwood): Yeah — there are three contributors: 1) raw throughput improvements: with dedicated GPUs and tuned kernels we get more tokens/sec per GPU; 2) batching efficiency: when many requests arrive concurrently we amortize per-request overhead, so tokens per GPU increase; 3) caching/prefix reuse: if you have repeated prompts or long conversations, KV cache avoids recomputation for prefix tokens. Quantization reduces memory and increases throughput too. Together, depending on your access patterns, that's the 2-4x.
[02:45] Daniel (Aurum): So if we say our target is $100k/month, how much throughput can we run? I know it's fuzzy.
[02:53] Maya (Redwood): Right — we'll run numbers after you share traffic. As an example, for a 13B-style model hosted, you might pay $0.10 per 1k tokens (example figure) — if you move to Dedicated with an effective 3x improvement you may get to ~$0.033 per 1k tokens equivalent. Those are illustrative; we'll provide exact spreadsheet rows.
[03:18] Priya (Aurum): That example helps. Embeddings are their own cost center — do you typically recommend separate Dedicated pools for embeddings vs generation?
[03:27] Noah (Redwood): Often yes, because embeddings have different latency/throughput tradeoffs and can be batched differently. You can also use lower cost model families for embeddings which improves unit costs.
[03:40] Owen (Aurum): On the security side, we have strict KMS and audit log needs. Private deployment or VPC is preferable for some data. How does that affect cost?
[03:50] Maya (Redwood): Private does add platform overhead and typically a base platform fee; Dedicated in a VPC still gives isolation with less overhead than full private on-prem. We'll share our SOC2 docs and KMS integration notes — that will show expected add-on pricing.
[04:05] Daniel (Aurum): Ok. For batching, what's the typical latency impact? We have product SLO of 300ms p95 for short prompts. Does batching break that?
[04:15] Noah (Redwood): Good question. We support dynamic batching with latency SLOs — you can set max queueing delay. Batching can improve cost without increasing tail latency if you cap wait time. For p95 300ms, you can still batch micro-batches; the cost savings are less extreme but still meaningful.
[04:35] Priya (Aurum): Any empirical numbers you can share here? Like cost improvement at 100ms vs 500ms max queuing?
[04:42] Maya (Redwood): In our benchmarks, going from 100ms cap to 500ms cap improved batching efficiency by ~1.5-2x on throughput in some workloads. But again depends on arrival pattern. We'll run a benchmark with your traffic to quantify.
[04:58] Daniel (Aurum): About caching — how effective is prefix/KV caching for our use case if we have long conversation contexts?
[05:05] Noah (Redwood): If you have stable system prompts or shared context across requests, hit rates can be 30-70% for prefix tokens — which massively cuts compute. If your conversations are mostly unique each time, hit rate is lower. We'll ask Priya for a sample of prompt overlap to estimate hit rate.
[05:22] Priya (Aurum): We do have a lot of boilerplate prompts plus user-specific content. I'd estimate maybe 40% reuse across sessions.
[05:30] Maya (Redwood): That would be high impact. Ok quick aside — are you running any private models on-prem?
[05:36] Daniel (Aurum): Not now. We run some internal models on prem for sensitive data but most is cloud. We could consider Private Redwood deployment later.
[05:44] Owen (Aurum): Network wise, we need VPC peering and customer-managed KMS. Any gotchas?
[05:50] Noah (Redwood): We support VPC peering and bring-your-own-KMS for Dedicated and Private. Key considerations: egress, subnet sizing, and firewall rules for gRPC endpoints. We'll put a short network checklist in the follow-up.
[06:05] Priya (Aurum): On quantization — is int8 production-ready for us? We care about quality.
[06:12] Noah (Redwood): Most of our quantized paths (int8) preserve generation quality for many open models especially after calibration. For strict quality SLAs we recommend running eval sets; Redwood Optimize gives model/quantization recommendations per workload. We'll help run small evals to check regression risk.
[06:30] Daniel (Aurum): Nice. Can we get a very concrete example: with our numbers (300 tokens, 30 r/s peak), if we did Hosted non-committed vs Dedicated reserved with a 6-month commit, what's the monthly cost difference?
[06:42] Maya (Redwood): We'll model that in the spreadsheet but illustrative: hosted pay-as-you-go could be higher in variable cost — you pay per token. Dedicated amortizes GPU commitment, so for steady high volume Dedicated is usually 25-60% cheaper after factoring in batching and caching. The exact breakpoint depends on utilization and traffic variance.
[07:05] Priya (Aurum): What's the typical commit size for Dedicated? We don't want to overcommit.
[07:10] Maya (Redwood): We have minimum entry points — e.g., 2-4 GPU pods depending on GPU type. We can do stepped commits and autoscale bursts. For your QPS, we probably need 4 A100-style GPUs as a starting ballpark, but we'll size more precisely after you send telemetry.
[07:26] Daniel (Aurum): Important question — how do we forecast cost for multi-model strategy? We'll use different models for cost vs quality tradeoffs.
[07:33] Noah (Redwood): We support model routing rules: lower-cost models for background tasks, high-quality models for critical tasks; Redwood can route by policy. This helps control unit economics by shifting load.
[07:45] Priya (Aurum): Do you expose token-level breakdowns per route?
[07:48] Maya (Redwood): Yes, Console shows token counts by model/route, cost per token, and per-route latency. Useful for chargebacks.
[07:58] Owen (Aurum): About the benchmark — what's required from our side?
[08:02] Noah (Redwood): Sample prompt set, traffic profile (QPS, concurrency, avg seq length, arrival distribution), desired latency SLOs, and any dataset access if you want semantic evals. We'll run a 48-72hr run and provide cost projections.
[08:17] Priya (Aurum): We can share a 2k prompt sample and QPS traces.
[08:21] Daniel (Aurum): Timeline — we want a pilot within two weeks. Is that realistic?
[08:25] Maya (Redwood): Yes, with the prompt sample and some basic network configs we can start next week. Noah will drive the bench.
[08:32] Priya (Aurum): A few nitty gritty things — how do you handle spikes for embeddings? We sometimes have big backfills that spike.
[08:40] Noah (Redwood): You can have separate dedicated pools with scheduled scaling and burst capacity; for hosted we provide burst autoscaling but it's subject to capacity. For heavy one-off backfills we recommend spot/ephemeral clusters or a batch job in Private.
[08:55] Daniel (Aurum): Competitors — we evaluated Anthropic's managed offering and also looked at self-hosting on EC2. Our concern is both cost and ops overhead.
[09:05] Maya (Redwood): Makes sense. Self-hosting can be cheaper at very large scale but has ops burden; Redwood aims to reach self-host economics while retaining managed ease. We'll surface a cost comparison.
[09:15] Priya (Aurum): Any risks we should watch for in the POC?
[09:19] Noah (Redwood): Main ones are: mismatch between sample traffic and production traffic, underestimating variability, and quality regressions if using aggressive quantization. We'll help instrument and measure.
[09:28] Daniel (Aurum): Great. Let's talk about invoicing — do you do monthly invoices for Dedicated?
[09:33] Maya (Redwood): Yes, monthly or annual billing. Reserved gives discount. We'll include billing cadence in the proposal.
[09:40] Priya (Aurum): Can you share a sample contract for Dedicated? Legal will want to review SLAs.
[09:45] Maya (Redwood): We'll include an initial term sheet and SLA summary.
[09:48] Owen (Aurum): Small thing — is there support for bringing our own model weights (we may have proprietary fine-tuned models)?
[09:55] Noah (Redwood): Yes, Dedicated and Private support customer weights; we can discuss security controls around that.
[10:00] Priya (Aurum): Ok good.

[10:05] Maya (Redwood): Quick recap then next steps: we'll send the per-token pricing spreadsheet with hosted vs dedicated examples and the network + KMS checklist; Noah will start a benchmark once you share prompts and telemetry; we'll also send SOC2 and security docs. Pilot kickoff target: 2026-03-09. Any other items?
[10:26] Daniel (Aurum): That covers it. Priya, Owen — ok?
[10:29] Priya (Aurum): Yep.
[10:30] Owen (Aurum): Yep.

(Transcription artifacts note: occasional mis-hears; product names sometimes recorded as "Redwood dedicated" vs "Redwood Dedicated"; numbers approximate.)

End of transcript.
